_meta.interpretation: Yes, clearly. Comparing each customer with themselves, revenue rose on average by roughly a quarter of the earlier level; the interval for that rise is narrow and well above zero, and the effect size is large. Pairing is what makes this sharp: each customer is their own baseline, so the wide differences between customers drop out. The test says spending rose, not why: the test period mixes the treatment with a gradual drift over time, so the rise belongs to both.
_meta.question: Did customers spend more during the test period than they did before it?
_meta.description: Paired t-test on the per-unit revenue lift (revenue vs revenue_before) to detect the average treatment effect.
_meta.name: paired_t_before_after
